content.text:
This Outlook Scheduling Assistant screenshot shows six attendees (Jamal Wright, Kenji Watanabe, Rachel Cohen, Grace Liu, Oliver Grant, Sofia Moreno) on Monday and Tuesday. Every row is drawn in that attendee's own local time against the time scale at the top: Oliver Grant's row (labeled London, GMT) is in London time, and every other row is in New York time (ET). ET = GMT - 5 hours on these dates. Each attendee can only meet between 9:00 and 17:00 in their own local time. Treat busy, tentative (hatched) and out-of-office blocks all as busy. What is the earliest 45-minute slot, starting on a quarter hour, when all six can attend? Give the start in New York time (ET) as the day and 24-hour time, in the form `Tue 09:45` (three-letter day, HH:MM with a leading zero).

Think step by step. Then end your reply with one final line in exactly this form:
FINAL ANSWER: <your answer>

message.content:
ET attendees’ working hours are 09:00–17:00. Oliver’s London working hours convert to 04:00–12:00 ET, so any shared slot must fall between 09:00 and 12:00 ET.

On Monday, the first 45-minute opening for the five ET attendees is 09:30–10:15, but Oliver is busy in London from 14:30 to 15:00 during that slot. On Tuesday, Sofia is busy until 10:00, so no earlier start works. From 10:00 to 10:45 ET, the five ET attendees are free, and Oliver is free from 15:00 to 15:45 London time.

FINAL ANSWER: Tue 10:00
